title: Cingulate Cortex Atlas
subtitle: Trace anterior, midcingulate and posterior cingulate functions
altText: Chalkboard-style anatomical atlas illustration highlighting the cingulate cortex atlas and its major connections.
learningObjectives: Identify the major components of the cingulate cortex atlas.
Trace key connections and functional relationships of the cingulate cortex atlas.
Relate lesions or network disruption to plausible clinical presentations.

sections.explainSimply: The cingulate cortex curves around the corpus callosum and helps connect motivation, pain, attention, memory and emotion.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Different cingulate zones participate in salience, action selection, autonomic regulation, error monitoring and internally directed cognition.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Anterior and midcingulate sectors connect strongly with prefrontal, insular, limbic, motor and autonomic systems; posterior cingulate and retrosplenial regions are central nodes in memory and default-mode networks. Boundaries are functional gradients rather than rigid boxes.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A bridge running around the brain’s central highway, linking body state, motivation, action and memory.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Cingulate lesions may alter initiation, error monitoring, affect, pain experience, memory orientation or self-referential processing depending on location and connectivity.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Damage or dysregulation can disrupt salience network, default mode network, pain matrix; presentations depend on laterality, extent and connected networks.
sections.clinicalPearl: “Cingulate dysfunction” is too broad to be clinically useful—specify the subregion, network and task demand.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician uses the cingulate cortex atlas map to test whether a patient’s pattern is anatomically coherent while considering broader network and medical explanations.
sections.limitationsCautions: Atlas localisation supports hypothesis generation, not diagnosis. Individual anatomy, distributed processing, compensation and comorbidity limit one-to-one structure–symptom claims.

anatomy.position: Integrated within deep or medial cortical-brainstem relationships shown in the atlas.

quiz.question: Which statement best describes the cingulate cortex atlas?
options: Different cingulate zones participate in salience, action selection, autonomic regulation, error monitoring and internally directed cognition.
It acts independently of the rest of the brain.
It has one fixed psychological function.
It can diagnose psychiatric disorders from anatomy alone.
quiz.rationale: The structure participates in distributed networks and should be interpreted in context.

quiz.question: What is the safest clinical inference from this atlas?
options: A lesion pattern can guide hypotheses but requires clinical and medical correlation.
One symptom proves one structure is damaged.
quiz.rationale: Neuroanatomy constrains hypotheses but does not replace assessment.

quiz.question: Why are connections important?
options: Symptoms can reflect disconnection and downstream network effects.
All pathways are identical across people.
quiz.rationale: Distributed cognitive systems depend on pathways linking regions.
